question: A salesman marks his goods 5% above the cost price and gives a discount of 40% on them. Find his loss percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the successive percentage change formula to directly find the net profit or loss.

Net change % = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, x = +5% (Markup) and y = −40% (Discount)

Net change % = 5 − 40 + (5 × −40) ÷ 100 = −35 − 200 ÷ 100

Net change % = −35 − 2 = −37% (The negative sign indicates a loss)

**∴ The correct answer is 37%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = +5%

Discount % = −40%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP + (Markup % of CP)

Selling Price (SP) = MP − (Discount % of MP)

Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100
